statements.label: supported
statements.text: To study enhancer control of senescence, the team generated time-resolved transcriptomes and epigenome profiles during oncogenic RAS-induced senescence.
statements.evidence: We explored this by generating time-resolved transcriptomes and epigenome profiles during oncogenic RAS-induced senescence and validating central findings in different cell biology and disease models of senescence.
statements.note: The abstract states this was the approach used to study senescence.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Pharmacologic AP-1 inhibition reduced tumour growth in mouse cancer models.
statements.evidence: Together, our findings enabled us to manipulate the senescence phenotype with potential therapeutic implications.
statements.note: The abstract notes therapeutic implications but never tests AP-1 inhibition on tumour growth in mice.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Activator protein 1 pioneers the senescence enhancer landscape and defines the organizational principles of the transcription-factor network driving senescent cells' transcriptional programme.
statements.evidence: We demonstrate that activator protein 1 (AP-1) 'pioneers' the senescence enhancer landscape and defines the organizational principles of the transcription factor network that drives the transcriptional programme of senescent cells.
statements.note: The abstract reports AP-1 pioneering the enhancer landscape and defining the TF network.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Integrative analysis and functional validation revealed links between enhancer chromatin, transcription-factor recruitment and senescence competence.
statements.evidence: Through integrative analysis and functional validation, we reveal links between enhancer chromatin, transcription factor recruitment and senescence competence.
statements.note: The abstract reports these revealed links as a result.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Natural killer group 2 member D ligands are up-regulated in senescent cells in vitro regardless of the stimulus that induced senescence.
statements.evidence: are up-regulated in senescent cells in vitro, regardless of stimuli that induced cellular senescence
statements.note: The abstract reports NKG2DLs up-regulated in senescent cells irrespective of the inducing stimulus.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mouse NKG2D-CAR T cells improved physical performance and alleviated multiple aging-associated pathologies in irradiated and aged mice.
statements.evidence: Targeting senescent cells with mouse NKG2D-CAR T cells alleviated multiple aging-associated pathologies and improved physical performance in both irradiated and aged mice.
statements.note: The abstract reports improved physical performance and alleviated pathologies in these mice.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Autologous human NKG2D-CAR T cells deleted naturally occurring senescent cells in aged nonhuman primates without any observed adverse effects.
statements.evidence: Autologous T cells armed with the human NKG2D CAR effectively delete naturally occurring senescent cells in aged nonhuman primates without any observed adverse effects.
statements.note: The abstract reports effective senescent-cell deletion in aged primates without observed adverse effects.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: NKG2D-CAR T-cell treatment extended the lifespan of the aged animals.
statements.evidence: Our findings establish that NKG2D-CAR T cells could serve as potent and selective senolytic agents for aging and age-associated diseases driven by senescence.
statements.note: The abstract reports senolytic efficacy and improved performance but never measures lifespan or survival.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The senotherapeutic intervention extended the lifespan of the treated old mice.
statements.evidence: Collectively, our data provide compelling evidence for cellular senescence as a hallmark and potentially tractable mediator of SkM aging.
statements.note: The abstract reports improved muscle strength but never measures lifespan or survival.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A subpopulation of old fibroadipogenic progenitors highly expresses p16 Ink4a and multiple senescence-related genes while showing DNA damage and chromatin reorganization.
statements.evidence: a subpopulation of old fibroadipogenic progenitors highly expresses p16 Ink4a together with multiple senescence-related genes and, concomitantly, exhibits DNA damage and chromatin reorganization
statements.note: The abstract reports this high expression and accompanying damage in old progenitors.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A senotherapeutic intervention improved skeletal muscle strength and countered age-related molecular and morphological changes in old mice.
statements.evidence: Administration of a senotherapeutic intervention to old mice countered age-related molecular and morphological changes and improved SkM strength.
statements.note: The abstract reports improved strength and countered age-related changes after the intervention.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The senescence phenotype is conserved in skeletal muscle from older humans.
statements.evidence: Finally, we found that the senescence phenotype is conserved in SkM from older humans.
statements.note: The abstract reports the senescence phenotype as conserved in older human skeletal muscle.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Itpr2 knockout mice displayed increased lifespan, a better response to metabolic stress, and less liver steatosis and fibrosis.
statements.evidence: Itpr2 knockout (KO) mice display improved aging such as increased lifespan, a better response to metabolic stress, less immunosenescence, as well as less liver steatosis and fibrosis.
statements.note: The abstract reports these features of improved aging in the knockout mice.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Cellular senescence is decreased in Itpr2 knockout mice and in knockout embryo-derived cells.
statements.evidence: Cellular senescence, which is known to promote these alterations, is decreased in Itpr2 KO mice and Itpr2 KO embryo-derived cells.
statements.note: The abstract reports decreased senescence in the knockout mice and their cells.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: A pharmacological ITPR2 inhibitor reproduced the lifespan extension seen in the knockout mice.
statements.evidence: These findings shed light on the role of contacts and facilitated exchanges between the ER and the mitochondria through ITPR2 in regulating senescence and aging.
statements.note: The abstract tests only genetic knockout and ablation, not a pharmacological inhibitor.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Ablating ITPR2 reduces the number of mitochondria-ER contacts, whereas forcing such contacts induces premature senescence.
statements.evidence: ablation of ITPR2 in vivo and in vitro decreases the number of contacts between the mitochondria and the ER and their forced contacts induce premature senescence
statements.note: The abstract reports fewer contacts on ablation and premature senescence on forced contacts.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Metformin produced a roughly 6-year regression in brain aging and significantly slowed aging indicators in the monkeys.
statements.evidence: The results highlighted a significant slowing of aging indicators, notably a roughly 6-year regression in brain aging.
statements.note: The abstract reports a significant slowing of aging indicators and a ~6-year brain-aging regression.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Metformin extended the survival of the treated monkeys.
statements.evidence: In a rigorous 40-month study, we evaluated the geroprotective effects of metformin on adult male cynomolgus monkeys, addressing a gap in primate aging research.
statements.note: The study ran 40 months and measured aging-clock indicators, but survival or lifespan was not an outcome.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Metformin had a substantial neuroprotective effect, preserving brain structure and enhancing cognitive ability.
statements.evidence: Metformin exerts a substantial neuroprotective effect, preserving brain structure and enhancing cognitive ability.
statements.note: The abstract reports neuroprotection, preserved brain structure, and enhanced cognition.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Metformin's geroprotective effects on primate neurons were partially mediated by activation of Nrf2.
statements.evidence: The geroprotective effects on primate neurons were partially mediated by the activation of Nrf2, a transcription factor with anti-oxidative capabilities.
statements.note: The abstract attributes the neuronal geroprotection partly to Nrf2 activation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Senescence-associated heterochromatin foci form in oncogene-induced senescence but are absent in replicative senescence.
statements.evidence: Differential intra- versus inter-SAHD interactions lead to the formation of senescence-associated heterochromatin foci (SAHFs) in OIS but not in RS.
statements.note: The abstract reports SAHF formation in OIS but not in RS.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: DNMT1 induces senescence-associated heterochromatin foci by promoting HMGA2 expression.
statements.evidence: We also identify DNMT1 as a factor that induces SAHFs by promoting HMGA2 expression.
statements.note: The abstract identifies DNMT1 as inducing SAHFs via HMGA2.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Depleting DNMT1 shifts oncogene-induced senescent cells toward a 3D genome conformation resembling replicative senescence.
statements.evidence: Upon DNMT1 depletion, OIS cells transition to a 3D genome conformation akin to that of cells in replicative senescence.
statements.note: The abstract reports this conformational transition on DNMT1 depletion.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Blocking SAHF formation restored proliferative capacity in oncogene-induced senescent cells.
statements.evidence: These data show how multi-omics and imaging can identify critical features of RS and OIS and discover determinants of acute senescence and SAHF formation.
statements.note: The abstract identifies SAHF determinants but never tests whether blocking SAHFs affects proliferation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Older specific-pathogen-free mice produce more IL-1a and IL-1b in steady-state bone marrow than young mice, mostly from myeloid cells.
statements.evidence: older specific pathogen free (SPF) wild-type (WT) mice in contrast to young SPF mice produce more interleukin-1a and interleukin-1b (IL-1a/b) in steady-state bone marrow (BM)
statements.note: The abstract reports more IL-1a/b in older than young mice, mainly from myeloid cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Blood from older mice contained higher levels of TLR4 and TLR8 ligands.
statements.evidence: blood from steady-state older SPF WT mice contains higher levels of microbe-associated molecular patterns, specifically TLR4 and TLR8 ligands
statements.note: The abstract reports higher TLR4 and TLR8 ligand levels in older mice's blood.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The microbiome/IL-1/IL-1R1 axis drives myeloid-biased hematopoiesis in aged humans.
statements.evidence: Collectively, our data define the microbiome/IL-1/IL-1R1 axis as a key, self-sustaining and also therapeutically partially reversible driver of HSC inflammaging.
statements.note: All experiments were performed in mice; human HSCs were not examined.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Antibiotic suppression of microbiota or pharmacologic IL-1 blockade reversed the myeloid-biased HSC output in older mice.
statements.evidence: in vivo antibiotic suppression of microbiota or pharmacologic blockade of IL-1 signaling in older WT mice was similarly sufficient to reverse myeloid-biased output of their HSC populations
statements.note: The abstract reports both interventions reversing myeloid-biased HSC output.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: A small-molecule KAT7 inhibitor reproduced the lifespan extension achieved by genetic KAT7 targeting.
statements.evidence: CRISPR-Cas9-based genetic screening is a robust method for systematically uncovering senescence genes such as KAT7 , which may represent a therapeutic target for developing aging interventions.
statements.note: KAT7 was targeted genetically via CRISPR and lentiviral vectors; no small-molecule inhibitor was tested.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: KAT7, a histone acetyltransferase, ranked as a top hit whose deficiency alleviated senescence in both progeroid hMPC models.
statements.evidence: including KAT7 , a histone acetyltransferase, which ranked as a top hit in both progeroid hMPC models
statements.note: The abstract reports KAT7 as a top hit whose deficiency alleviated senescence in both models.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Inactivating KAT7 decreased histone H3 lysine 14 acetylation and repressed p15 INK4b transcription.
statements.evidence: Inactivation of KAT7 decreased histone H3 lysine 14 acetylation, repressed p15 INK4b transcription, and alleviated hMPC senescence.
statements.note: The abstract reports decreased H3K14 acetylation and repressed p15 INK4b after KAT7 inactivation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Intravenous Cas9/sg-Kat7 extended lifespan in physiologically aged mice and in progeroid Zmpste24-/- mice.
statements.evidence: lentiviral vectors encoding Cas9/sg- Kat7 , given intravenously, alleviated hepatocyte senescence and liver aging and extended life span in physiologically aged mice as well as progeroid Zmpste24 -/- mice
statements.note: The abstract reports extended lifespan in both mouse models after intravenous Cas9/sg-Kat7.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Single-cell RNA sequencing of 20 organs mapped cell-type-specific responses to young and aged blood in heterochronic parabiosis.
statements.evidence: Here we performed single-cell RNA sequencing on 20 organs to reveal cell-type-specific responses to young and aged blood in heterochronic parabiosis.
statements.note: The abstract reports scRNA-seq across 20 organs to study parabiosis responses.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Heterochronic parabiosis extended the lifespan of the aged mice.
statements.evidence: Together, these data lay the groundwork for a systemic understanding of the interplay between blood-borne factors and cellular integrity.
statements.note: The abstract reports transcriptomic changes but never measures lifespan or survival.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Aged blood reduced global gene expression, whereas young blood restored it in select cell types.
statements.evidence: aged blood reduces global gene expression, and young blood restores it in select cell types
statements.note: The abstract reports aged blood reducing and young blood restoring global gene expression.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Adipose mesenchymal stromal cells, haematopoietic stem cells and hepatocytes were among the most responsive cell types.
statements.evidence: Adipose mesenchymal stromal cells, haematopoietic stem cells and hepatocytes are among those cell types that are especially responsive.
statements.note: The abstract names these cell types as especially responsive.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: SIRT2 is required for HSC maintenance and regenerative capacity in old age by cell-autonomously repressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation.
statements.evidence: SIRT2, a cytosolic NAD + -dependent deacetylase, is required for HSC maintenance and regenerative capacity at an old age by repressing the activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome in HSCs cell autonomously.
statements.note: The abstract reports SIRT2 maintaining old HSCs by cell-autonomously repressing the NLRP3 inflammasome.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: With age, SIRT2 expression falls and mitochondrial stress rises, driving aberrant NLRP3 inflammasome activation in HSCs.
statements.evidence: With age, reduced SIRT2 expression and increased mitochondrial stress lead to aberrant activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome in HSCs.
statements.note: The abstract reports reduced SIRT2 and increased mitochondrial stress driving NLRP3 activation with age.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: SIRT2 overexpression, NLRP3 inactivation, or caspase 1 inactivation improves the maintenance and regenerative capacity of aged HSCs.
statements.evidence: SIRT2 overexpression, NLRP3 inactivation, or caspase 1 inactivation improves the maintenance and regenerative capacity of aged HSCs.
statements.note: The abstract reports each of these manipulations improving aged HSC function.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: SIRT2 overexpression extended the overall lifespan of the aged mice.
statements.evidence: These results suggest that mitochondrial stress-initiated aberrant activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome is a reversible driver of the functional decline of HSC aging and highlight the importance of inflammatory signaling in regulating HSC aging.
statements.note: The abstract reports improved HSC function but never measures organismal lifespan.
